source_text: hédan. Add: I. to take charge or possession of (with gen.). (1) the object a person :-- Gif hé næbbe mǽgburg, héden his þá gefán, Ll. Th. i. 148, 19. (2) the object a thing. [Hml. Th. ii. 114, 33 : Exod. 583 : Ll. Th. i. 436, 9: Hml. Th. i. 330, 31 in Dict.] II. to have a care for, take notice of (with gen.) [B. 2697 : Ll. Th. ii. 316, 30 : Hml. Th. iv. 534, 16 in Dict.] III. to care for, take notice of (with acc.) [Hml. Th. ii. 116, 4 in Dict.] IV. to take care that (with clause) :-- Héde sé ðe scíre healde þ-bar; hé friðige and forðige ǽlce be ðám ðe hit sélest sý, Angl. ix. 259, 13. V. to observe, take note of (gen.) :-- Næs him ná þe sél þæs þe hé georne hédde, ne mihte hé þǽr nǽnne geseón þe hé gecnáwan cúþe, Hml. S. 23, 638. Gelamp hit þ-bar; sume hlosniende menn ðǽr betweónan eódon and þisra seofona georne héddon, 137.
